answer: Reputation escrow with delayed release. Each identity accrues a score that unlocks rewards only after a dawn settlement delay, so a cluster of clones cannot consolidate value before operators are traced. If fraud is detected, the operator's entire identity graph is frozen, including the meadow of dormant accounts it controls, forcing attackers to sacrifice all linked history at once. The unlock schedule also requires periodic crystal-clear proof-of-work linking each account to a distinct hardware fingerprint, raising per-clone cost above the reward.
